newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL KEEP IN TOUCH WITH LEADERS UNITED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL KEEP IN TOUCH WITH LEADERS UNITED.

text.p: Liverpool closed to within three points of English premier league leaders Manchester United on Monday with a controversial 2-1 win at third-placed Arsenal.
The relegation battle between Middlesbrough and Nottingham Forest ended 1-1.
The first half at Highbury was a high-speed affair with little time on the ball for either side.
Liverpool's Stan Collymore missed three decent chances while Dennis Bergkamp blazed over for Arsenal.
But five minutes into the second half Collymore was presented with an unmissable opportunity when David Seaman failed to hold a shot by Stig Inge Bjornebye.
Seaman, playing his first game after nearly two months out injured, was heavily involved in the second Liverpool goal in the 65th minute.
He was penalised for bringing down Robbie Fowler in the box -- despite the Liverpool player doing his best to convince the referee that there was no contact.
Seaman then saved Fowler's poorly-struck penalty -- only for Jason McAteer to bang in the rebound.
Ian Wright pulled one back 12 minutes from time but it was too late for Arsenal who stayed six points behind United from a game more.
Liverpool manager Roy Evans said he thought his side deserved to win a "very competitive game". "It's a tough place to come and win," he said.
However, he refused to accept the championship is now a two-horse race.
"Anyone who thinks that is crazy," he said. This game has kicked people in the teeth all season."
Evans said he was unaware that Fowler had tried to tell the referee it should not have been a penalty, but added: "If that's what he did then he's very honest."

In the important relegation duel at the Riverside Stadium, Alf-Inge Haaland put visiting Forest ahead after four minutes, driving the ball home after Pierre van Hooydonk's shot had been parried by Mark Schwarzer.
Mikkel Beck equalised for Middlesbrough in the 56th when he touched in Neil Cox's cross.
Forest move above Coventry into 18th place -- still in the relegation zone -- while Middlesbrough are one place above.
